body:
WHAT
Every JSON state file is written by writing to `<file>.tmp` and then renaming it over the target, with a remove-then-rename fallback for Windows. The engine uses writeFileAtomic (settings.json, graph.json, symbols.json, task store); the app uses writeJsonAtomic (config.json, profiles.json, workspace and global settings.json). An optional mode (0600) is applied to the temp file and re-applied after rename.

WHY
The app SIGKILLs the engine 3 s into shutdown and both processes write settings.json; a truncated file reads as 'no settings', which looks like a workspace that lost its endpoint and key.

WHERE
engine/core/src/util/fsAtomic.ts — export function writeFileAtomic(file, data, mode?) (mkdirSync, writeFileSync tmp, renameSync with rmSync fallback, chmodSync best-effort); callers engine/core/src/config/settings.ts (setSetting → writeFileAtomic(file, …, 0o600)), engine/core/src/knowledge/graph.ts, engine/core/src/knowledge/symbols.ts, engine/core/src/state/taskStore.ts. app/main/config.js — writeJsonAtomic(file, value, mode) used by writeConfig(), updateWorkspaceSettings(); app/main/profiles.js writeProfiles() → writeJsonAtomic(profilesPath(), list, 0o600); app/main.js clearGlobalSettingsKeys() → writeJsonAtomic(globalSettingsPath(), …, 0o600).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. writeFileAtomic and writeJsonAtomic each leave no '<file>.tmp' behind after success and the target parses as the full JSON written.
2. If renameSync throws once (simulated EPERM on Windows), the fallback removes the target and renames again, and the final content is the new value.
3. With mode 0o600 on an existing world-readable target, the result file has mode 0600 (skipped on Windows) and a missing parent directory is created.
4. A grep over app/main*.js and engine/core/src confirms no direct fs.writeFileSync of a path ending in settings.json, graph.json, symbols.json, profiles.json or config.json outside the two helpers (the .env writer in connection.js is the documented exception).
5. Reading the target concurrently while a write is in flight (in a loop of many writes) never observes an empty or unparseable file — readSettingsFile returns either the old or the new object.
